history.dynasty: Ancient sacred site; present structure built 1780 by Maratha queen Ahilyabai Holkar
history.period: Ancient site (Skanda Purana); present temple 1780; Kashi Vishwanath Dham Corridor 2021
history.summary: One of the 12 Jyotirlingas, on the western bank of the Ganga at Varanasi, praised in the Skanda Purana's Kashi Khanda and believed to grant moksha. Its history is a cycle of destruction and rebuilding: demolished in the Ghori/Aibak invasion (1194), rebuilt, rebuilt again by Raja Man Singh / Todar Mal under Akbar (1585), and demolished in 1669 by Aurangzeb, who built the Gyanvapi Mosque on its site. The present temple on an adjacent site was built in 1780 by Maratha queen Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore; in 1835 Maharaja Ranjit Singh donated about a tonne of gold to plate the dome. In December 2021 the Kashi Vishwanath Dham Corridor connecting the temple directly to the Ganga was inaugurated, sharply increasing pilgrim numbers. name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
town_description: Varanasi (Banaras/Kashi) is one of the world's oldest living cities, on the banks of the Ganga in eastern Uttar Pradesh. India's spiritual capital, it is famed for this Jyotirlinga, its ghats, the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, Banaras Hindu University, silk weaving and classical music.

travel.airport: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi (approx. 25 km; prepaid taxis, app cabs, airport bus).
travel.railway: Varanasi Junction / Cantt (approx. 4-5 km; 15-20 min by auto/taxi), well connected across India.
travel.road: In the old city's narrow lanes near Dashashwamedh Ghat; reach by auto/rickshaw to Godowlia Chowk, then walk through Vishwanath Gali (10-15 min), or enter via the Corridor from the Ganga side. Kashi Darshan Bus Seva stops nearby.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. Visit 4:00-7:00 AM for calmer darshan; evening aarti is energetic but crowded. Maha Shivaratri and Shravan Mondays see extreme crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open approx. 2:30/3:00 AM to 11:00 PM daily. General darshan (free): morning 4:00-11:00 AM, afternoon 12:00/12:20-7:00 PM. Five daily aartis: Mangala 3:00-4:00 AM, Bhog 11:15 AM-12:20 PM, Sapta Rishi 7:00-8:15/8:30 PM, Shringar/Bhog 9:00-10:15 PM, Shayan 10:30-11:00 PM. Paid Sugam Darshan (approx. INR 250) and aarti passes; advance booking via shrikashivishwanath.org. No mobiles/cameras, remove leather items, carry ID proof.
